clue.text: Teachers having a job removing boy from lesson

parts.note: a post is a job or position

indicators.note: taking something away, so the boy's letters come out of the word lesson

parts.note: a son is a boy

explanation.surface: Teachers with jobs are pulling a lad out of class.
explanation.definitionFit: The apostles were the first teachers of Christ's message, sent out to spread it.

clue.text: Number reportedly supporting fratricide

parts.note: pro means for or in support of

indicators.note: reportedly means as heard, so a word is spelt how it sounds

parts.note: Cain killed his brother Abel in Genesis

explanation.surface: A figure is said to back a brother's murder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Number' is not a figure but something that numbs: procaine is a local anaesthetic.
explanation.definitionFit: Procaine is a local anaesthetic, something that deadens sensation, so a numb-er.

clue.text: He wrote lines in various motets

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the other
various suggests different arrangements, so the letters of motets are mixed

parts.note: L is an abbreviation for line, so LL means lines

explanation.surface: A man wrote words for a variety of church choral pieces.
explanation.walkthrough: 'various' rearranges the letters of motets into SMOETT before the lines go in.
explanation.definitionFit: Tobias Smollett was an 18th-century Scottish novelist, author of Roderick Random.

clue.text: Bird left safe haven during flood

parts.note: Noah's Ark kept its occupants safe during the Flood

explanation.surface: A bird flew from a refuge as the waters rose.
explanation.definitionFit: The lark is a songbird, famed for the skylark's song.

clue.text: Mass panic at horse-riding accident

indicators.note: panic throws things into disorder, so the letters of mass are rearranged

parts.note: horse is slang for heroin, abbreviated H
a jockey riding a horse is said to be up

explanation.surface: Mass panic at a horse show causes a collision.
explanation.walkthrough: 'panic' rearranges MASS as SMAS; 'at' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A smash-up is a violent collision, especially of vehicles.

clue.text: Manages to find time for some monkey business when US girlfriend comes over

indicators.note: in a down clue, coming over means sitting above the other piece

parts.note: squeeze is American slang for a girlfriend
a sin is a bit of wrongdoing

explanation.surface: Someone fits in a quick fling when their American girlfriend visits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'when' is a link; in a down clue the girlfriend sits on top of SIN.
explanation.definitionFit: To squeeze something in is an idiom for fitting it into a busy schedule.

clue.text: Porter concealing love affair was very noticeable

indicators.note: concealing means hiding within, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: porter is a dark beer, like stout
love is zero in tennis, so O
a do is a party or social affair

explanation.surface: A hotel porter hiding a romance was conspicuous.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Porter' looks like a doorman but is the beer.
explanation.definitionFit: To stand out is to be prominent or conspicuous, so stood out means was very noticeable.

clue.text: Will provider examine list of names drawn up?

parts.note: to test is to examine

indicators.note: in a down clue, drawn up reads the word from the bottom upwards, reversing it

parts.note: a rota is a list of people on duty

explanation.surface: Someone making a will checks the roster of beneficiaries prepared.
explanation.definitionFit: A testator is a person who has made a will, so the one who provides it.

clue.text: Model friend entertains mum when one's gone away

indicators.note: to entertain a guest is to hold them within, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: a mate is a friend

indicators.note: something gone away has been removed, so one letter drops from the word before

parts.note: mum, as in 'keep mum', means quiet
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A model's friend has their mother round while somebody is away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mum' looks like a mother but means silent, as in 'keep mum'; 'gone away' leaves QUET once the I goes.
explanation.definitionFit: A maquette is a small preliminary model made by a sculptor before the full work.

clue.text: Indian state in drama about a danger zone

parts.note: Noh, also spelt No, is classical Japanese drama
Goa is a state on India's west coast
re means about or concerning

explanation.surface: A play set in an Indian state is about a perilous place.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is a link here, not a container: the pieces sit side by side.
explanation.definitionFit: A no-go area is a district thought too dangerous to enter, hence a danger zone.

clue.text: Enquire into English getting swamped in naval attack

indicators.note: being swamped is being engulfed, so one letter sinks inside the other piece

parts.note: a sea bout is a fight at sea

explanation.surface: Investigating an Englishman overwhelmed during a sea battle.
explanation.walkthrough: E goes inside SEA BOUT, after the S, to give SEE ABOUT.
explanation.definitionFit: To see about something is to look into it or deal with it, an idiom for investigating.

clue.text: Excited when contacted by phone

definitions.meaning: a buzz is a thrill, so to be given one is to be excited
a buzz is also slang for a phone call

explanation.surface: Someone gets thrilled when a call comes through.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses play on buzz: a thrill, and informal slang for a telephone call.

clue.text: Top golfer's card?

parts.note: a leading golfer could be called a champion with clubs, and the phrase also names a playing card of the black suit

explanation.definitionFit: The highest card in the club suit; read playfully, the best player with golf clubs.

clue.text: Roof space full of these boxes

indicators.note: to box something is to enclose it, so these words hold the answer within them

explanation.surface: An attic crammed with cardboard boxes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'boxes' looks like the contents of the attic but is the verb: the words full of these contain the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A loft is the space directly under a roof, used for storage.

clue.text: Uncultured ambassador assigned to capital city briefly

parts.note: HE, His Excellency, is the title of an ambassador

indicators.note: a word said briefly is cut short, losing its final letter

parts.note: Athens is the capital of Greece

explanation.surface: A boorish diplomat is posted to a capital for a short time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'assigned to' is a link; Athens, cradle of culture, makes a nice irony with 'Uncultured'.
explanation.definitionFit: Heathen is used loosely to mean uncivilised or lacking culture, beyond its religious sense.

clue.text: Tough guy is a challenge to legal team?

definitions.meaning: a difficult lawsuit is tough for the lawyers arguing it

explanation.surface: A thug's trial is a tough job for his lawyers.
explanation.definitionFit: A hard case is slang for a tough person, and literally a difficult court case.

clue.text: Solved a burglary right away, as may be proved

indicators.note: something solved has been worked out, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A detective cracked a break-in straight away, as evidence may show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'right away' says R is removed from the letters of A BURGLARY before they are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Arguably means as one could argue or show, a sense close to provably.

clue.text: Book used in church by extremely pious convert

indicators.note: the extremes of a word are its first and last letters

parts.note: to convert is to alter

explanation.surface: A devout person converts using a church book.
explanation.definitionFit: A psalter is a book containing the psalms, used in church services.

clue.text: In sum, no limits to English applicants worthy of consideration

indicators.note: in means one piece goes inside another

parts.note: a lot is an amount or sum, as in 'the whole lot'

indicators.note: with no limits a word loses its first and last letters

explanation.surface: In short, there is no cap on English applicants deserving a look.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sum' looks like arithmetic, but here a lot is a total amount.
explanation.definitionFit: A longlist is the initial set of candidates shortlisted from before final selection, those worth considering.

clue.text: Dead ringer for one 'making eulogy

parts.note: ex means former, no longer living or active
a toller is one who tolls a bell

explanation.surface: A spitting image of someone delivering a tribute.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dead ringer' reads as a lookalike, but the phrase splits in two; 'for' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who extols another praises them highly, as a eulogy does.

clue.text: How reporter might identify himself, to make good effect

definitions.meaning: a journalist announcing 'I am from the newspapers', contracted
to make a strong favourable impression

explanation.surface: A journalist introduces himself to win people over.
explanation.definitionFit: To impress is to make a good impression on someone; I'm press is a reporter's introduction.

clue.text: Piece for piano — a composition by Indian?

parts.note: a rag is a ragtime piece, typically written for piano

explanation.surface: A piano work wonders if it was written by an Indian composer.
explanation.definitionFit: A raga is a melodic framework for improvisation in Indian classical music, so a composition by an Indian.

clue.text: Iron skirt with tiny movement that's what one expects of a woman

definitions.text: that's what one expects of a woman

parts.note: Fe is the chemical symbol for iron
a mini is a short skirt

indicators.note: movement shifts the letters of tiny around into a new order

explanation.surface: Ironing a skirt with a small motion is thought of as womanly.
explanation.definitionFit: Femininity is the set of qualities traditionally associated with women.

clue.text: Author's chapter given to manager

parts.note: a handler manages someone, like an agent or trainer

explanation.surface: A writer's chapter is passed to their manager.
explanation.walkthrough: 's is 'is' and 'given to' a link joining the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Raymond Chandler was an American writer of hardboiled detective novels.

clue.text: Destroy penguins' food source, when river vanishes

indicators.note: something that vanishes is taken away, so its letter goes

parts.note: krill are tiny crustaceans eaten by penguins and whales

explanation.surface: Wiping out the penguins' prey when a river dries up.
explanation.definitionFit: To kill is to destroy life.

clue.text: Qualified priest's unkind remark about introduction to liturgy

parts.note: Eli is the priest who raised Samuel in the Old Testament

indicators.note: about here means round, so the taunt goes round a letter

parts.note: a gibe is a taunt

indicators.note: an introduction is the opening, so take the first letter

explanation.surface: A priest's barbed comment concerning the start of a service.
explanation.definitionFit: Eligible means fit or entitled to be chosen, hence qualified.

clue.text: In programme, supporter's written about coach

indicators.note: about signals turning round, so the letters are written in reverse order

parts.note: an ally is a supporter; with the 's it gives allys
a coach is a bus

explanation.surface: A programme note in which a fan writes about the team coach.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' turns ALLYS into SYLLA; 'In' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A syllabus is a programme of study for a course.

clue.text: Royalist travelling alone

indicators.note: travelling moves things about, so the letters of Royalist are rearranged

explanation.surface: A monarchist is journeying solo.
explanation.definitionFit: Solitary means being alone, without company.
